item.title: Declan Rice strikes late for Arsenal to deny Bayern Munich in blockbuster
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013 , although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa maintain perfect start against Viking
item.description: “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” read the pre-match display held up by the Holte End. Even if few would really be ready for a full-on repeat of 1982, when Aston Villa conquered Europe, the current vintage are doing an outwards impression of Champions League contenders. The small blot here was that they would have ended the night top of the 36-team table until Peter Christiansen, with an acrobatic volley awarded by the video assistant referee, scored a consolation for Viking that the Norwegian champions’ second-half display merited. By then Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendía had, in a first half of near-embarrassing dominance from Villa, virtually guaranteed the result before Henrik Heggheim’s own goal had Villa briefly looking down on the entire continent. item.title: Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation
item.description: Bruno Fernandes was taken off in the 67th minute in Como [Getty Images] Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes turned on head coach Michael Carrick following one of the most humiliating nights in the club's European history. A 4-1 Champions League hammering at Como led to Carrick fielding questions about his future. He apologised to the 700 travelling fans, having ignored his beaten players after the final whistle to march across the pitch and repeatedly hold his hands up - in a manner similar to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer following a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021 which led to his dismissal as United boss 24 hours later. However, Fernandes - widely accepted as a football obsessive who watches games regularly as he understands the tactical side as well as any player in the United squad - inflicted more damage when he spoke to TNT Sports afterwards. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," he said. Asked directly whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable." Told of Fernandes' comments in his post-match press conference, Carrick offered a curt response: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." Man Utd embarrassment in Como leaves Carrick job in danger Carrick avoids questions on future, apologises to fans for unacceptable display Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick acknowledges the club's fans after the 4-1 defeat by Como [Getty Images] Carrick also refused to answer questions about his own future. Instead, he described his own feelings about United's performance and focused on taking responsibility. "I have to apologise to the supporters," said the former player. "I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more, with the position that I'm in and what I value this football club. For us to play in that way is not acceptable. "I always go over to the fans anyway, regardless, so it wasn't a particularly different kind of reason why I went over. "It's the appreciation and acknowledgement of what they've gone through and have done over a period of a few weeks now. As I said, I was one of them. "I'm feeling the same as them. We've got a lot of values in this football club; what we represent and how we want to go about it. We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight wasn't acceptable. Seven without a win - Man Utd's bleak picture Carrick was appointed permanent boss on a two-year contract in May [Getty Images] After winning 12 of his 17 games in charge last season to guide United back into the Champions League after a two-year absence, Carrick was given a two-year contract. However, as happened with Solskjaer five years ago, the new campaign has unravelled spectacularly and they are 13th in the Premier League, three points clear of bottom club Sunderland. It is a basic reality that if Como's star man Nico Paz, who opened the scoring after 118 seconds, created the second and added a third goal, said he wanted to leave Como, virtually every big club in Europe would want to sign him and United's chances would be virtually non-existent. They entertain 15th-placed Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday knowing that prior to last season's amazing 4-4 draw, the Cherries recorded 3-0 wins on their previous two visits to Old Trafford. What happens now? United flew straight back to Manchester after the game. It remains to be seen whether the position around Carrick changes before the Bournemouth game. However, United supporters sang against the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe as the shambolic evening unravelled. Both Carrick and sporting director Jason Wilcox have been absolved of partial blame for the club's plight by some; Carrick because he was let down badly in the summer transfer window, when the club signed three midfielders, but failed to bring in competition for Luke Shaw at left-back and Benjamin Sesko in attack. Wilcox too, because he had to work to a budget set by those above him, including chief executive Omar Berrada. "There was a lot going through my mind watching that," admitted Carrick, who won five Premier League titles and the Champions League during his United playing career. "It was tough to watch. "It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was was the manner and way we played at times. "I'm giving my absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life is wrapped around it. item.title: Galo youngsters play for a place in the final on Saturday
item.description: Galo youngsters play for a place in the final on Saturday Atlético drew 0–0 with Cruzeiro on Wednesday (21) at Arena MRV in the first leg of the 2026 Brazilian Under-17 Championship semifinal. In a derby with chances for both teams, goalkeeper Guilherme Pires was one of the standouts for the young Galo side, making important saves throughout the match. The result leaves the battle for a place in the final wide open. The decisive match will take place next Saturday (24) at 3 p.m. at Arena do Jacaré in Sete Lagoas. A win will send Atlético through. Another draw will take the tie to a penalty shootout. The reigning Brazilian champions at this age level, Galo are looking to reach their second consecutive final and stay in contention for back-to-back national titles. 🐓 The match The derby got off to a lively start at Arena MRV. Atlético relied on some fine work from Guilherme Pires, who made important saves to deny the opposition. In the 19th minute of the first half, Atlético's defense stepped up again at a crucial moment. After a shot from inside the six-yard box, Alexsandro cleared the ball off the line , preventing the opening goal. The young Galo side looked to respond in attack, mainly through Gabriel Veneno and set pieces, but neither team scored before halftime. For the second half, coach Rafael Paiva brought on Ricardo Filipe in place of João Guilherme. In the 58th minute, the coach made three more changes, bringing on Vieira, Barros and Pedrinho for Alexsandro, Lukaku and Gabriel Veneno, respectively. In the closing stages, João Heleno and Moisés Caetano also came on, replacing Callegario and Gomide. Atlético stayed organized defensively and relied on Guilherme Pires' assured goalkeeping to finish the first leg of the semifinal with a clean sheet. The 0–0 draw leaves a place in the final to be decided in the second leg. 🏆 Chasing back-to-back titles Atlético reached the Brazilian Under-17 Championship semifinal after knocking out Palmeiras in the quarterfinals. In the first leg at Arena MRV, the young Galo side won 3–0. In the return leg in Barueri, Vinicius Rodrigues scored for Atlético to secure qualification with a 4–3 aggregate score . The result put Atlético among the top four clubs in the national competition for the second year running. In 2025, Galo won the Brazilian Under-17 title by beating Grêmio in a final decided on penalties. Now, Rafael Paiva's team are looking to advance once more and keep their hopes of back-to-back titles alive. 📅 Next match Atlético return to action on Saturday (24) at 3 p.m. against Cruzeiro at Arena do Jacaré in Sete Lagoas, in the second leg of the Brazilian Under-17 Championship semifinal. After the goalless draw at Arena MRV, Galo need a win to reach the final. Another draw will see the tie decided on penalties. The Boston native returned to the Rangers in 2015-16, the final season of a five-year contract that he signed in 2011 as a member of the Coyotes. New York again reached the postseason, but only won a single game in the playoffs, bowing out in five games to the Pittsburgh Penguins in the best-of-7 first round series.. As expected, Yandle was full of hilarious stories and one-liners, including a wild story about a prank that he and Kevin Hayes pulled with the Rangers on up-and-coming young forward J.T. Miller . The conversation also included some interesting insight from Yandle about his decision to leave New York, and how he ended up in Florida without ever technically becoming an unrestricted free agent. “Luckily for me that summer, the UFA d-men were like me, [Brent] Seabrook, [Dustin] Byfuglien, there might have been one other guy, and all of those guys had signed with their teams during the year,” Yandle explained. “And, I was kind of the biggest name left.” As it turns out, Yandle already weighed his options for where he would land next, and someone in his circle was singing the praises of the Panthers for quite some time. When I was in Florida, it seemed like every month, someone was in town, so it made a lot of sense logistically.” The logic behind the change in location was sound, as was the desire to be a veteran on an up-and-coming team. Yandle was entering his age-30 season at the time, and likely viewed Florida as a team that was on the verge of competing for championships. “I didn’t want to re-sign in New York, just because I saw the team kind of going down a little bit,” Yandle said. “Guys were leaving. “I never even got to [unrestricted free agency]. New York offered me [a contract], and I said no. And then, they asked me where I wanted to sign, and I told them Florida, so they traded my rights to Florida. So, I never even was a UFA. We got it done before July 1.” You can watch the full exchange here: Yandle played the next five seasons in Florida, totaling 231 points in 371 regular-season games. On July 15, 2021, the Panthers bought out the final two seasons of the seven-year contract he signed back in 2016. He went on to play 77 games with the Flyers in 2021-22, finishing with a shocking minus-47 plus/minus mark, and retired following that season. Along the way, Yandle put together the longest Ironman streak in NHL history, playing 989 consecutive games between March 26, 2009, and March 29, 2022. Since he retired, two players passed his record — Phil Kessel (1,064 consecutive games played) and Brent Burns, whose active streak sits at 1,017 straight games. item.title: Fernandes laments 'mood of defeat' as Man Utd crumble in Como
item.description: Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United endured a difficult evening in Como (PIERO CRUCIATTI) Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said his side lacked belief as their woes continued with a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club's winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. "We started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," Fernandes told TNT Sports. "Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way." The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz's early strike for Como had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. "Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat," said Fernandes. "It's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. "If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Fernandes also highlighted United's passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick's tactics, Fernandes said: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. "Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable." Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield, admitted the display was simply not good enough. "We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night," said Tielemans. "You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor." mw/jc/iwd

item.title: Championship-winning Jacksonville baseball coach to retire in summer
item.description: Bishop Kenny head baseball coach Tommy Edwards will retire from coaching after the 2027 spring season, the athletic department announced Oct. 21, which will end one of Jacksonville's most successful and consistent active coaching tenures on the diamond. The school has designated former Bishop Kenny player and current assistant coach KK Daniel as his successor. Edwards has spent 33 years with Bishop Kenny as a player, assistant coach or head coach. He will be entering his 22nd season at the helm this spring, having taken over from longtime Crusaders coach Bob West after the 2005 high school season. During his time at Bishop Kenny, Edwards has led the team to 16 Florida High School Athletic Association district championships, three final-four appearances and the state championship in 2008. Times-Union records show a career mark of 387-191 in Edwards' Crusaders career. Daniel, the Crusaders' coach in waiting, has served on Bishop Kenny's staff for the past six years. He played baseball at the school from 2010 to 2013 and competed in college at Florida Gulf Coast, Cowley County Community College and Drury University. Bishop Kenny is scheduled to compete in FHSAA District 4-4A in 2027 alongside Englewood, Fleming Island, Menendez, Parker, St. Augustine and Westside. item.title: Dodgers Exec Being Considered For 2 Managerial Openings
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers executive Rocco Baldelli is a frontrunner for the managerial jobs opened by the Houston Astros and Seattle Mariners this offseason. The Mariners relieved manager Dan Wilson of his managerial duties following the close of the 2026 season, as did the Astros with manager Joe Espada. With Baldelli’s managerial experience, it’s only natural the 45-year-old is drawing attention from the rest of the league. What Qualifies Rocco Baldelli to be a Manager? Baldelli, who played in the majors from 2003-2010 with the Tampa Bay Rays and Boston Red Sox, got his start in managing in 2019 , when he took over the Minnesota Twins nearly a decade after his playing career ended. He won 101 games in his first season as a manager with the Twins, earning the AL Manager of the Year award, though his team lost in the first round of the postseason without winning a game. He won his first postseason game with the team in 2023, snapping an 18-game losing streak in the postseason. After that, though Baldelli failed to get his team into the postseason. Mandatory Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images He remained with the team through the 2025 season, finishing his time as the manager with 527 wins to 505 losses. The Twins finished 2025 with a 70-92 record in 2025, leading to Baldelli’s dismissal. After the Twins fired Baldelli, the Dodgers signed him on as a special assistant to president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, with whom he formed a professional relationship while playing for the Rays. Are the Astros and Mariners the Only 2 Teams After Baldelli? The Astros and Mariners are the only two teams reported to be in on Baldelli, but a third team could enter the mix shortly after letting go of their manager. The Los Angeles Angels declined to pick up manager Kurt Suzuki’s option for the 2027 season on Wednesday, opening up a spot as the team’s manager for the second time in as many years. The Angels are sure to give Baldelli a look, especially given his proximity to the team. Baldelli, a proven manager, will definitely draw the eyes of teams across the league, managerial opening or not, so the Dodgers may have trouble holding on to him beyond the 2026 season.

item.title: ‘Angry’ Michael Carrick responds to questions on Man Utd future after Como calamity
item.description: Michael Carrick has insisted that he is not considering his future after Manchester United ’s humbling 4-1 defeat to Como left him on the brink. United were thrashed by Cesc Fabregas ’ side in their third Champions League outing of the season, extending the club’s winless run to seven. Carrick’s position as United manager is now clouded by uncertainty but as the former Red Devils reflected on his side’s performance, he declared that speculation surrounding his job was not what he was focussing on. “I’ve not given my position any thought,” he told a press conference. “It’s [about] the supporters, I was one of them, and I didn’t like what I saw.” Michael Carrick was left ‘angry’ with his Man United side after being humbled by Como (AP) Speaking to TNT Sports in a separate interview, Carrick echoed the same sentiment and said “it’s not about me” when asked if he still expected backing from the cliub. Carrick took “100 per cent responsibility” for how the team performed but nevertheless expressed his anger and frustration at the level he witnessed, apologising to the travelling supporters for the latest dismal result. "I'm really angry but you've got to move on and deal with what's next and see what that looks like,” he said. "At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before the next game to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everybody. "It's not about playing for me - it's about playing for this football club. It’s the responsibility what comes with it. I’m in the position, I’m responsible for the club and the supporters. "I’m giving my absolute best all the time. My whole life's wrapped around it [Man Utd]. It might go well, it might not go so well, but I genuinely give everything I possibly can. "It's not about me and the relationship, it's about what we all give, players, staff, for this football club.” Carrick also responded to Bruno Fernandes’ criticism of his tactics, specifically their lack of pressing which gave Como too much time and left them somewhat toothless. "We half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that,” he said. "Whatever tactics you play, it you don't run back, you ain't going to win." Man United’s next outing comes on Sunday as they host Marco Rose’s struggling Bournemouth in the Premier League.

item.title: “You can’t choose when you want to…”: Carrick aims damning accusation at United stars after Como humiliation
item.description: “You can’t choose when you want to…”: Carrick aims damning accusation at United stars after Como humiliation Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has turned the spotlight on his own players after their Como collapse on Wednesday. Defeat United found themselves behind after just two minutes as Nico Paz curled home a fantastic effort past Harry Maguire. Paz then turned provider, registering an assist for Tasos Douvikas’ strike moments after the break. Paz secured his brace on the hour mark before defender Jacobo Romano headed home Como’s fourth. Substitute Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal for United in stoppage time. The Red Devils are now on a seven-match winless run as pressure on Carrick continues to mount. Como were in Serie D when United last won the Champions League in 2008, but they were by far the better side, with Carrick’s men unable to get near them. Speaking to reporters after the final whistle, Carrick acknowledged that United are in a hole. He also tore into the work ethic of his players, stressing that they can’t choose when to work hard and when not to. Carrick, in remarks that appeared to question the players’ commitment, additionally insisted that the ultimate responsibility rests with him. Carrick’s remarks The United head coach said, “It was more than disappointing; everybody’s gotta take responsibility for that.” “It stops with me, I’m absolutely fine with that. I accept it totally as a supporter of this football club. I care a lot about it. To see a performance like that is unacceptable.” He continued, “There were all sorts of elements to our performance. I’ll definitely look at what we’ve done [as a staff]. I don’t know if it’s the motivation, intention, purpose, and intensity of a football game that you have to bring — we didn’t bring that today.” Asked if United are simply only capable of performing at the current level, he answered, “100% it’s not our level.” “We’ve shown it for six or seven months [last season] but you can’t turn it on or off and you can’t choose when you want to perform or don’t want to perform. Until you do that, you’re not going to win football matches.” Carrick issued an apology to the travelling supporters. “I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They are the heartbeat of this football club and always will be. For them to travel, I’ve gotta apologise for the performance.” “For everything they’ve done to get here tonight, to have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them.”

item.title: Sensational USMNT star could be heading to Liverpool
item.description: Sensational USMNT star could be heading to Liverpool Liverpool could be on the verge of signing an exciting player. January is just around the corner. It may seem like a long distance away but we are almost approaching Halloween. Soon there will be Christmas decorations in every shop. Your favourite and least favourite Christmas songs will be chiming out from every radio and speaker wherever you go. And then, it's January and the proper football transfer season is underway. For Liverpool, these windows have been quiet in general. There's been the odd big transfer, but mostly Liverpool prefer to do their business in the summer. This time though things could be different. This time Julian Ward could go on a big spending spree as there are multiple areas to fix in the squad. So, strap yourself in and get ready for an exciting winter. Liverpool's exciting plans for January Last January, Liverpool got some big deals over the line. They agreed three future transfers for three exciting centre-backs. Mor Talla Ndiaye joined the Reds immediately. Meanwhile, Jeremy Jacquet and Ifeanyi Ndukwe arrived at the club in the summer after agreeing moves in the winter. This time around, naturally Liverpool are going to be exploring the market for these type of transfers as well. Gilberto Mora is very much on the club's radar as a potential new signing. However, he is not the only one who Liverpool will pursue. They will also weigh up their options in the midfield. Lamina Camara is a long-term target who could be available and Ward's exciting plans could involve bringing him to Anfield. The bottom line is that the Reds will be busy. Justin Ellis could be heading to Liverpool We wrote recently about a potentially interesting development of Justin Ellis' alleged social media account posting a picture at Liverpool's training ground. Now Ellis is one of the most exciting young USMNT prospects breaking through the ranks. A forward who can play out wide on the right and as a no.10 as well, he recently scored two goals in his first three games for the US' senior national team. For Orlando this season, he has three goals and 12 assists in 28 appearances, and has stood out with his playmaking ability. The way he plays is similar to Roberto Firmino, and with his contract expiring in June 2027, it would make sense that Liverpool would be interested in him. He is 19-years-old, proving himself at senior club and international level and with such short-terms on his contract this is a move that screams textbook Julian Ward. He likes bringing in young versatile players with elite potential. Ellis is exactly that, and it's why he could be heading to Liverpool.

item.title: Steelers Release Veteran Safety Before Paris Game In Latest Shake-Up to Secondary
item.description: Steelers Release Veteran Safety Before Paris Game In Latest Shake-Up to Secondary originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The reshaping of the Steelers ' secondary will continue into Week 7. A few weeks after trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, with safety DeShon Elliott likely to return from injury soon, Pittsburgh announced it is cutting ties with a veteran safety on Wednesday. Rayshawn Jenkins will hit free agency after struggling with the Steelers over the first six games of the 2026 season. Here's what to know about Jenkins' release and what it means moving forward. Steelers Release Veteran Safety In Latest Shake-Up to Secondary The Steelers announced the release of Jenkins on Wednesday after he played in all six games for the team so far, including one start. However, for the most part, Jenkins — a 10-year veteran who has had stints with the Chargers, Jaguars, Seahawks and Browns — struggled to emerge as a starter despite his experience, with 562 total tackles, 11 interceptions, 5.5 sacks and 34 pass deflections in his career. After starting all 17 games for the Browns last season, Jenkins landed with the Steelers in the offseason, but was quickly replaced by seventh-round rookie Robert Spear-Jennings in the starting lineup. Per Steelers Now , Jenkins was targeted five times before his release from Pittsburgh, allowing five completions for 120 yards, one touchdown and a perfect 158.3 passer rating. For the Steelers, the move likely indicates that they didn't have a need for Jenkins because Elliottt will return soon, out since October 2025 with hamstring/knee injuries. Elliott had a setback in the preseason and was unable to start the season for the Steelers. Elliott's 21-day practice window was opened on Oct. 8, and head coach Mike McCarthy has remained hopeful that he'll be back on the field soon. Whether Elliott will be ready for the Paris matchup against the Saints remains to be seen, but he's likely to return at some point soon. item.title: Dream hoping for Rhyne Howard breakout in WNBA Finals Game 3
item.description: Dream hoping for Rhyne Howard breakout in WNBA Finals Game 3 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Rhyne Howard had a historic Game 2 of the WNBA Finals -- and surprisingly, it had nothing to do with her offense. Howard, the Atlanta Dream 's All-Star guard, had an offensive rating of 74 in Saturday's Game 1 and 79 in Monday's Game 2. She has scored 17 points from 21 shot attempts through two games -- but Atlanta has evened up the Finals anyway. That's in part due to Howard's Finals-record six steals in Monday's 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries , which sends the series south to Atlanta for the next two games in what has become a best-of-five series. MORE : Rhyne Howard makes WNBA Finals history in game that barely shows up in scoring column The Dream has flourished this postseason and enters Game 3 on Wednesday night with a 6-1 playoff record. Atlanta is two wins from a first-ever championship despite Howard's offensive struggles: the four-time All-Star is shooting only 30.6 percent from the floor in the playoffs, though her defense remains outstanding. She was a first-team All-Defense selection, after all. Got to chop it up with Karl Smesko during shootaround this morning! On Rhyne’s early struggles, PnR volume vs off-ball usage, the risk/reward of rim attempts in this series and more. https://t.co/QgJrX5xUCH — Nekias (Nuh-KAI-us) Duncan (@NekiasNBA) October 21, 2026 Still, Dream head coach Karl Smesko feels a breakout might be close if Atlanta continues to punish Golden State in transition, as was the case in Game 2. "I think the more we get out in transition, I think it'll help Rhy get easier looks," Smesko said Wednesday from State Farm Arena. "(The Valkyries) are obviously pretty focused on not losing her and not letting her have any separation. ... We want Rhy to be a big part of what we do." Howard will remain a fundamental part of the Dream's plan while Atlanta hopes her shot will come around. If it does, the Valkyries defense will have more than just Angel Reese to worry about. While we don’t really know what Wiggins is as an OC at this point in his career, I expect the Aggies to come at Alabama with a very similar gameplan as what Tennessee did: Run the ball and throw quick screens. For one, they will want to protect Marcel Reed from giving Alabama freebie. And for two…. Well, it worked for the Vols, why not do the same thing? While Reed and the running backs will get some rushing yards on the Tide defense, I have trouble seeing how this offense can really threaten the Tide too much, unless the Alabama offense just gives them ball in good field position over and over (which is definitely not out of the realm of possibilities). I think the Alabama defense mostly self-corrects some of their flaws from a week ago, though the questionable nature of Zabien Brown’s injury may affect things. Still, I think that this is an OC that is probably out of his league against a more experienced Kane Wommack, and there’s been nothing to suggest that Marcel Reed won’t continue to self-sabotage. So let’s go with 12-14 points for the Aggies. Roll Tide

item.description: Cubs' All-Star outfielder is a 'realistic' free agent target for Phillies originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies could have a very busy offseason. After another disappointing postseason showing, Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski will likely be hoping to add impact players, especially on offense. Philadelphia scored just nine runs in its three Wild Card Series games against the Atlanta Braves . The front office could also look to make defensive upgrades, as the Phillies were well below par on that side of the ball. Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly believes that makes left fielder Ian Happ a "realistic" free agent target for the Phillies. He hit 24 home runs and posted 10 defensive runs saved in 2026. "Additionally, with Bryce Harper returning to first base, Philadelphia needs an impact outfield bat. Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki are the big fish, but Ian Happ may be a more realistic target. "He has a .783 career OPS and is a four-time Gold Glove Award winner, so he could upgrade the defense of a team that finished tied for dead last in baseball, minus-51 defensive runs saved," Kelly wrote. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player Happ's strong outfield defense is something coveted by most organizations, including the Chicago Cubs . Given the Phillies' defensive struggles, it would make sense for them to find more sure-handed players who they know they can rely on. If the Cubs decide to bring back only one of Happ and Seiya Suzuki, either player may be on the Phillies' radar. item.title: Jim Nantz jokingly compares himself to Manny Pacquiao after viral Peanut Punch fail with J.J. Watt on live broadcast
item.description: Jim Nantz jokingly compares himself to Manny Pacquiao after viral Peanut Punch fail with J.J. Watt on live broadcast appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This past weekend, Jim Nantz tried to punch a football out of JJ Watt during the Las Vegas Raiders and Buffalo Bills game, and he paid for it, comparing himself to famous boxer Manny Pacquiao . Nantz appeared on The Pat McAfee Show to provide an update on his hand. He conceded that he went “a little too aggressive” with his Peanut Punch attempt. “Some are saying that it was the greatest punch thrown in Vegas since Pacquiao a few years back,” he joked. “I gave it my best, and as soon as I did it, I regretted it, because I felt like everything had been compressed, and I did think I was gonna wake up Monday with this thing [his wrist] about triple the size. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’m not gonna be on the injury report this week. I’m gonna be good to go, no broken bones,” he continued. "I did go a little too aggressive with the peanut punch on @JJWatt and it did sting.. I gave it my best and as soon as I did it I regretted it.. I'm not gonna be on the injury report this week and I'm good to go" ~ Jim Nantz #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/qZ5GI4tZaO — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 20, 2026 Even Josh Allen reached out to Nantz after the game. A former United States president also reached out, and Pat McAfee theorized that it was Barack Obama. Nantz tried his best to knock the ball out of Watt’s hand. He seemingly earned his respect for going as hard as he did, even if his attempt was unsuccessful. It’s unlikely he will try a similar stunt this week. Nantz is 30 years older than Watt, and his hands can’t be taking such a beating. At least he doesn’t have a brace on it. Nantz and Watt are paired in the booth this year after Tony Romo’s OWI arrest . This led Romo and CBS Sports to “mutually part ways” after nine years. Romo, a former NFL quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys, was the network’s lead color commentator for nearly a decade. The OWI arrest allowed his seat to open up, and Watt has replaced him for this season. In six weeks, he has already given viewers a memorable moment with Nantz’s Peanut Punch attempt. item.title: ‘Our best player’ – Real Madrid fans continue to heap praise on midfield star vs RB Leipzig
item.description: ‘Our best player’ – Real Madrid fans continue to heap praise on midfield star vs RB Leipzig Supporters of La Liga giants Real Madrid have taken to social media in numbers on Wednesday evening, to sing the praises of a member of the club’s midfield ranks. The player in question? Arda Güler. Real Madrid are of course currently locked in action on the continent, in a Champions League meeting with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig. As things stand in Spain’s capital, Los Blancos find themselves headed towards another three-point haul, leading Leipzig by two gols to nil. The aforementioned Arda was afforded a starting berth for the evening, just rewards for a wonderful opening goal en route to Real Madrid’s weekend victory over Sevilla. And safe to say, the Turk has since fully rewarded the faith showcased by head coach José Mourinho. After laying on the assist for Bernardo Silva’s opener, Arda then turned goalscorer himself during the 2nd-half. And such excellence has not gone at all unappreciated on the part of his side’s fanbase, with some of a Real Madrid persuasion having gone as far as to label the 21-year-old Los Merengues’ very best player. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.description: “It’s a decision from the staff”: Bruno Fernandes puts the dagger into Michael Carrick after Como embarrassment Manchester United were thrashed 4-1 by Como in the Champions League as Michael Carrick’s time at the helm seems to be almost at an end. Cesc Fabregas’ side ran rings around the 20-time English league champions, who were laborious both with and without the ball. Bruno Fernandes calls out Carrick Just like Lisandro Martinez’s shocking interview after the Atletico Madrid defeat last week, this time it was Bruno Fernandes’ turn on Wednesday. The club captain called out the head coach and his staff for their lack of tactical clarity and his words made it seem like the poor performance was largely down to the former United midfielder. Speaking to TNT Sports , the Portugal international explained, “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them. “But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated. item.title: Big 22 Finalist: East Lincoln’s Jaxon Dollar
item.description: East Lincoln tight end Jaxon Dollar has been making headlines all season with eye-popping stats. Heading into last week’s win over Hickory, Dollar had posted 60 catches for over 1,100 yards and 15 touchdowns, including a six-touchdown performance against West Iredell. That performance, though, was in a loss, which means he had to hear it from the opposing sideline, getting a heavy dose of chirping. “If they’re winning, they say whatever they want. It’s usually just, ‘You’re trash.’ I’m not even bothered by it anymore, but it’s funny because it’s like, if you want to call me trash, you’ve got to at least lock me up, but nobody’s done that yet,” Dollar said. Nobody’s done it, no matter the coverage. Last Friday against Hickory, there was a double-team on every snap, sometimes even a second safety over the top to help the traveling corner. It can be frustrating at times for the future Georgia Bulldog, but Dollar has learned to be patient. “Last year, I wanted the ball every play. Who doesn’t? But just knowing that if I don’t get the ball, my team still wins. It’s a win in the books regardless. No matter if I have 12 touchdowns in a game and we lose, it’s still a loss. So as long as we get the win, that’s all that matters,” Dollar said. Voting for our Player of the Year ends next Monday at 10 a.m.

item.title: Carrick slams ‘unacceptable’ Man United performance against Como: ‘No excuses’
item.description: Carrick slams ‘unacceptable’ Man United performance against Como: ‘No excuses’ Michael Carrick was not best pleased with what he saw from his Manchester United players during their 4-1 defeat away against Como in the Champions League on Tuesday night, slamming an ‘unacceptable’ performance but insisting that ‘I 100% take responsibility, it stops with me’. Goals from Nico Paz (x2), Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon sent Como 4-0 up against Manchester United at the Stadio Sinigaglia on Wednesday evening, former Bologna forward Joshua Zirkzee pulling back a late consolation in injury time. You can see how the action unfolded on the Football Italia Liveblog. Carrick critical after Como 4-1 Manchester United ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammates during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) When he spoke ahead of kick-off, Carrick siad that he wanted to see his players take control of the game, but in the end, they were bettered in terms of possession, passes made, completed, pass accuracy, shots and shots on target. “It was more than disappointing,” the United head coach said after the full-time whistle. “I think everybody has got to take responsibility for that. I 100% take responsibility for the overall team and the performance – that’s where it stops. It stops with me and I’m absolutely fine with that. I accept that totally. “But as a supporter of this football club for so long, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say.” Carrick had to apologise in front of the traveling Manchester United fans who had remained in the stadium until the end of the game. Many of them packed up and left at 4-0. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, reacts after during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters,” said Carrick. They are the heartbeat of this football club and they always will be. “For them to travel, I had to apologise for the performance. To have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them. There are no excuses at all. It is not acceptable.” Carrick was also asked if he feels he has the backing of the Manchester United board, to which he replied: “It’s not about me. It’s about digesting the game and how it went. That is the most important thing right now.”

item.title: Warriors’ Steve Kerr makes prediction on his retirement alongside Stephen Curry, Draymond Green
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Warriors’ Steve Kerr makes prediction on his retirement alongside Stephen Curry, Draymond Green appeared first on ClutchPoints . While Golden State Warriors veterans Stephen Curry and Draymond Green adjust amidst the final stages of their respective careers, head coach Steve Kerr is doing the same. Much like the future Hall of Fame players he’s guided for over a decade, Kerr can’t say when he’ll retire from coaching . It’s a subject in which his feelings towards have changed over the years. Kerr addressed his future with the Warriors, per ESPN’s Wright Thompson. “I don’t want to go too late and I don’t want to go too early,” Kerr said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When head coach Steve Kerr was asked whether walking away from the Warriors after the 2025-26 season was too soon, he was uncertain. “I didn’t know. I didn’t know until I took those two, three weeks if it was too early. And then after talking to my wife, talking to Mike and Joe and Kirk [Lacob] and really examining what it would look like going forward, I came to the conclusion that, no, it was too early,” Kerr explained. “I still have something to offer. “And I think the team they have shown that they still want me here, and we still make a really good group. I’m talking about management, players, and coaches. And I’m so excited about this team, this season, our training camp. So I know without a doubt, it’s too soon, but I don’t want to be too late.” With two years left on his contract with the Warriors, Kerr envisions himself coming back for at least one more season in 2027-28. Then, perhaps retiring alongside the Warriors’ longest-tenured players — Stephen Curry and Draymond Green . “I signed for two years and I can’t see myself walking away after this year, but it feels now like there’s some shape to this thing,” Kerr said. “There’s some clarity. I could see this ending where Steph, Dray, we all leave around the same time. I could see that happening.” Kerr will begin his 13th season with the Warriors with an Opening Night matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday. item.title: ESPN’s top NBA crew dismisses possibility of NBA shortening regular season
item.description: Credit: ESPN As more and more NBA players sit out games due to load management, the league has been actively exploring ways to combat the issue, such as eliminating back-to-backs attached to nationally televised games and fining teams for sitting players in those contests. One frequently proposed, and rather simple, solution from players and fans has been to shorten the length of the 82-game season. However, ESPN’s top NBA broadcast crew doesn’t see it happening in the near future. “We play the same schedule that they’ve played [since the 1967-68 season], so what is going on? We’ve spent hundreds of millions of dollars in sports science, so what’s going on?” game analyst Richard Jefferson said on a preseason press call with reporters . “The players have more resources, more trainers, more planes, more equipment, all of the stuff. The quality of the product is how players are taking care of themselves, how they’re doing things. There are not as many back-to-backs, [and] less practice days, so that ‘Ferrari’ stays in the garage until race day. …You are disrespecting the older players that were doing back-to-backs on commercial planes with one equipment manager. It’s like, how easy do we want to make this?” Tim Legler largely agreed with Jefferson, noting that even with a shortened schedule, key players would find ways to rest ahead of the playoffs, reducing the opportunities fans would have to see the game’s stars. “In an 82-game season, our expectations right now of how much we’re going to see guys has changed. You’re not expecting 82. You’re praying for 70 and realistically you’re going to get 65,” Legler said. “Say you played a 70-game season. I don’t think you then see guys play 65, 70 games. You’re going to have a lot of guys play 60 games. Maybe 58 becomes the number. Now there’s even fewer nights when you’re seeing the top guys. …You’re just hoping you can get the top guys upright and healthy on April 15 for a two-month playoff run because it still will be the salvation of the NBA season.” Mike Breen, who has served as ESPN’s lead play-by-play voice since 2006, focused on the economic ramifications of reducing the games played, before ultimately arriving at the same conclusion as his colleagues. “It’s never going to happen,” Breen asserted. “Everyone is going to have to take less money. Ten games away to make it 72. That’s a lot of revenue over 10 games, and not just players, coaches, owners. How about all the peripheral people that work those games? Whether you work in the arena, whether you have businesses around the arena that rely on those 41 home games to make sure they pay their bills, etc. I think it impacts so many people in so many different ways financially that I don’t ever see it happening.” The post ESPN’s top NBA crew dismisses possibility of NBA shortening regular season appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Golfweek October Classic: Illinois Wesleyan banks a win to take into the offseason
item.description: Winning as an individual and winning as part of a team is not an apples-to-apples comparison. This is something Jim Ott, head men’s golf coach at Illinois Wesleyan since 2000, knows well. As Ott also noted, sometimes the experience of falling short down the stretch teaches all the lessons needed to get it done the next time. Ott’s team lived both of those adages on Oct. 20 as the Titans won the Golfweek October Classic in their fifth and final fall start. “You just can’t do it overnight, it takes time,” Ott said. “You almost have to be there – we always say, you have to throw up on yourself a couple times to figure it out and understand what it takes to win. “It’s different than winning individually. Winning as a team is a different level of pressure. If you fail yourself, it’s just yourself. But the guys are really close and have a team-first culture, it makes a difference when they know they’re playing for their teammates and not necessarily for themselves.” Last spring, Illinois Wesleyan was runner-up at the NCAA Division III National Championship. item.description: PITTSBURGH, PA - SEPTEMBER 16: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates rounds the bases on his two-run home run in the fifth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at PNC Park on September 16, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The current state of the Washington Nationals’ offense, especially after the trade deadline departures of Luis Garcia Jr. and Curtis Mead, is heavily driven by the dynamic duo that is James Wood and CJ Abrams. The lineup does include a handful of decent complementary pieces, including Keibert Ruiz and Daylen Lile, but is lacking both consistency and depth. Financial frustrations have led to Abrams and Wood’s names being floated in trade discussions, both hypothetical and legitimate, and their long-term futures with the team remain uncertain. Prospects like Eli Willits and Seaver King will look to break into the big leagues and give the MLB roster a boost, but relying on minor leaguers to carry the weight of a lineup that hopes to play in October is far from a sure thing. The trade market could help, but Washington’s low payroll gives them no excuse not to add offensive pieces in free agency. The roster’s need to bolster the pitching rotation indicates that much of the front office’s offseason focus will be directed toward arms, but President of Baseball Operations Paul Toboni could lean on his growing pitching pipeline and be more aggressive with free agent hitters. If, and that’s a big if, they choose to play ball with some of the bigger bats available, former Pittsburgh Pirate Brandon Lowe is a player that could really intrigue the Nats’ brass. Lowe is coming off his best statistical season to date based on bWAR, cruising past his previous high of 4.6 with an impressive 5.4 in 2025. The 9-year veteran absolutely raked after being traded to Pittsburgh, appearing in 150 games and putting up a .260/.331/.493/824. slash line and mashing 35 home runs with 96 RBI. Brandon Lowe crushed his first season in Pittsburgh 🏴‍☠️ pic.twitter.com/pnChU2Dv5a — MLB (@MLB) September 29, 2026 Washington has solid power output if all of their big-time hitters are clicking at the same time, but adding a bat like Lowe could instantly raise both the ceiling and floor of the offense. He’s eclipsed the 30-HR mark in every season he’s played over 110 games in, and has been a 110 OPS+ bat in all but one year. His 3rd percentile Whiff% wouldn’t do much to improve the Nats’ strikeout issues, but he has the pop to out-slug any concerns in that area. Addressing the position fit with Lowe, the 32-year-old has the ability to play 2B, fill in at 1B, or become the primary DH to maximize his offensive output. item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
